newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill rates higher but no takers.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill rates higher but no takers.

text.p: Manila banks quoted higher bid and offer rates for Treasury bills at the secondary market in reaction to the raising of the Central Bank's closely-watched overnight rate, traders said.
But there were no takers for the bills due to uncertainty over how long the Central Bank's rates will remain high.
On Wednesday, the Central Bank implemented a nine percentage- point increase in its overnight borrowing rate to 24 percent after the peso was hit by speculation from Thailand's de facto devaluation.
"Everybody is trying to sell. We don't know how long this will last," a foreign bank dealer said. "We don't want to fund these bills and borrow at 24 percent."
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave offers of 10.90/12 percent for one-month bills; 11.50/12.375 percent for the six months; and 11.80/12.725 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate soared to 24.3125 percent from 15.09375 percent, with the high at 26 percent.
"Borrowers in the market would have to pay the price because banks only want to lend to Central Bank at 24 percent," a dealer said.
The market, however, had 32 lenders and 19 borrowers. Volume was at 20.2 billion pesos.
